Connect to Databricks

databricks.Rmd

Databricks workspaces speak Spark Connect, so zuspark can query them directly: no databricks-connect, no Python and no JVM. You need the workspace’s URL, a personal access token, and one extra header that tells Databricks which compute to run on. This article shows serverless compute, which is all that Databricks Free Edition offers and which needs no cluster to be started.

library(zuspark)

Get a workspace URL and a token

The workspace URL is the start of the address in your browser while you are in the workspace, up to the domain, such as https://dbc-1a2b3c4d-5e6f.cloud.databricks.com. Leave out the path and the ?o= part.

To create a token, click your avatar in the top right corner, then Settings, Developer, and Manage next to Access tokens. Generate a new token and copy it: Databricks shows it only once.

Keep both out of your scripts. One way is to put them in ~/.Renviron, which R reads at start-up:

DATABRICKS_HOST=https://dbc-1a2b3c4d-5e6f.cloud.databricks.com
DATABRICKS_TOKEN=dapi...

Connect to serverless compute

spark_connect_databricks() reads DATABRICKS_HOST and DATABRICKS_TOKEN, and connects to the workspace’s serverless compute:

con <- spark_connect_databricks()
spark_version(con)

spark_version() reports the Spark version of the Databricks runtime behind the session. Serverless compute starts by itself when the session connects, and the first query can take a few seconds while it does.

What it does is plain Spark Connect: TLS on port 443, the token as a bearer token, and an x-databricks-session-id header carrying the session id. Without that header, the server answers “Invalid compute mode headers”. The same connection with spark_connect():

host <- sub("^https://", "", Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_HOST"))
session <- as.character(zuid::uuid(version = 4))

con <- spark_connect(
  sprintf("sc://%s:443/;use_ssl=true", host),
  token = Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_TOKEN"),
  session_id = session,
  headers = c("x-databricks-session-id" = session)
)

Run SQL

From here on, a Databricks session works like any other Spark Connect session:

q <- spark_sql(con, "SELECT id, id * 2 AS twice FROM range(5)")
spark_schema(q)
spark_collect(q)

Tables in Unity Catalog are queried by their three-part names, such as those of the samples catalog, where a workspace has it:

spark_collect(spark_sql(con, "
  SELECT pickup_zip, count(*) AS trips
  FROM samples.nyctaxi.trips
  GROUP BY pickup_zip
  ORDER BY trips DESC
  LIMIT 5
"))

Spark’s errors arrive with their error class and SQLSTATE, and spark_error_details() asks the workspace for the rest:

err <- tryCatch(spark_sql(con, "SELECT * FROM no_such_table"), error = identity)
err$error_class
err$sql_state
spark_error_details(err)[[1]]$message

Disconnect

spark_disconnect() releases the session on the workspace, so its serverless compute can stop:

spark_disconnect(con)

Classic compute

On a workspace with clusters (not Free Edition), give the cluster’s id. zuspark then sends it in an x-databricks-cluster-id header instead of the session header. The cluster must be running. This path has not been run against a real cluster yet:

con <- spark_connect_databricks(cluster_id = "0123-456789-abcdefgh")
